title: Elastic connection pools and staged degrade playbook for downstream resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement an adaptive connection pooling and staged degradation strategy for critical downstreams (Redis, Kafka, primary DB) to preserve SLOs during spikes and multi-region failovers. This ticket captures the design, rollout plan, decision points, and follow-ups for runtime changes: dynamic pool resizing, token-bucket ingress limits, per-backend circuit breakers, and progressive degradation modes (cache-only, read-only, sampled responses, simplified ranking).
decision_record: 1) Circuit breakers: per-backend CBs implemented in the runtime with sliding-window error rate and consecutive-failure thresholds. Trip threshold set to 30% error rate over 60s AND 25 consecutive failures for noisy endpoints. Half-open probe window uses 5 single requests spaced at 2s intervals. 2) Pool sizing: adopt exponential moving average of recent connection acquisition latency and queue depth to resize pools. Min and max caps per region to avoid runaway resource usage. 3) Load-shedding hierarchy: prefer graceful client-level reroutes (lower fidelity model or cached response) before returning hard 503s. 4) Multi-region failover: primary region marked unhealthy when regional health score < 60 for 90s; traffic shifts using weighted routing with gradual 10% steps and canary probes. 5) Metrics and SLOs: align actions to error budget consumption—if weekly error budget < 25% trigger immediate conservative degrade mode.
slo_details: SLO targets: availability 99.9% (per-region), p50 latency < 120ms, p95 latency < 300ms for API generation endpoints. Downstream error budget: 0.1% of requests per week for downstream-induced errors. Degradation triggers tied to: (a) downstream 5xx spike causing >0.5% of requests to fail in 5m window, or (b) sustained p95 downstream latency > 1.5x baseline for 2 windows.
playbook_steps: 1. Detect: runtime emits per-backend health score using latency+error rate. 2. Isolate: open CB for dependency; drain queued requests to a short-circuit path. 3. Route: shift traffic away from region/dependency using weighted policy and probe endpoints. 4. Degrade: apply staged modes — A: cache-only for reads; B: read-only with write queueing + background write drain; C: sampled responses for non-critical endpoints; D: fallback to smaller/faster model for ranking. 5. Recover: half-open probes, progressive pool warmup, rollback of temporary changes and post-mortem.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity: dynamic pools and CB tuning increase surface area for bugs and require strong observability.
- False positives: aggressive CB thresholds can cause unnecessary failovers; conservative settings delay mitigation.
- Consistency: degrading to cache/read-only may expose eventual consistency windows for customers.
- Cost: multi-region reroute and extra probes increase cross-region bandwidth and compute.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing runtime health API (metrics exported to prod-metrics) and extend with per-backend moving-average latency.
- Connection pool implementation: token-bucket admission + prioritized queue. When queue depth exceeds 75% trigger background warmup of extra connections up to max.
- Circuit breaker: store CB state in local process with optional sync to central control plane for observability.
- Load-shedding: implement a per-route policy layer that can mark requests as degradable via metadata flags; adopt quick path for cached responses.
- Testing: chaos experiments using staged failure injection (redis latency, kafka timeouts, db connection saturation) in staging and canary clusters.

rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback if: (a) application p95 latency increases by >35% vs baseline and not attributable to failover, (b) customer-facing error rate increases >0.5% within 10 minutes after deploy, or (c) critical endpoints (login/payment) see any 5xx spike >0.1%.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for CB transitions and pool resize logic.
- Integration test harness simulating connection saturation and slow reads.
- Staging chaos: inject 200-500ms additional latency on Redis and observe degradation path.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 1 hour, 20% for next 2 hours, then full rollout if all signals OK.
